questions.question: Why does reducing curvature in the path from noise to data help a generative model sample faster?
options: Straighter paths can be integrated accurately with far fewer numerical steps
Curved paths make neural networks impossible to train
Straight paths remove the need for any learned model
Curvature only affects training memory, not inference
questions.explanation: The lesson motivates flow matching by contrasting curved diffusion trajectories with straighter transport paths. If the path is close to linear, a simple Euler solver can move from noise to data in only a few steps instead of dozens.

questions.question: In a diffusion-style sampler, what does the model fundamentally need in order to update a noisy sample toward data?
options: A direction or velocity telling it how to move the current sample
A list of all training examples in memory
A nearest-neighbor search over the dataset at every step
A second decoder that converts text straight into pixels
questions.explanation: Before the lesson-specific details, the core intuition is that iterative generation needs an update direction at each state. Flow matching makes that direction explicit by training a vector field v_theta(x, t) to point along the transport path.

questions.question: What target does conditional flow matching regress against along the straight-line interpolant x_t = t x_1 + (1-t) x_0?
options: The denoised sample x_0 itself
The constant velocity x_1 - x_0
The covariance matrix of the dataset
The classifier-free guidance weight
questions.explanation: The lesson defines the straight-line path between noise x_1 and data x_0, then differentiates it to get dx_t/dt = x_1 - x_0. Training is simply mean-squared regression of the learned vector field onto that velocity target.

questions.question: Why is flow-matching training described as simulation-free in the lesson?
options: Because it never requires a neural network
Because training directly samples (x_0, x_1, t) and regresses a velocity target without unrolling the ODE
Because inference uses only one step
Because it uses a lookup table instead of gradient descent
questions.explanation: The lesson explicitly notes that you do not simulate the trajectory during training. You just sample endpoints and a time t, form x_t analytically, and fit the model to the corresponding target velocity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rectified flow's reflow procedure?
options: To generate text captions for training images
To convert the model into a GAN discriminator
To iteratively create ODE-matched pairs that make the learned trajectories flatter and easier to sample in 1-4 steps
To replace Euler integration with beam search
questions.explanation: Rectified flow trains an initial model, uses it to produce matched start-end pairs, and then retrains on those pairs. The lesson says this iterative straightening makes the ODE closer to linear, enabling high-quality 2-4 step inference.
